references.text: Reference to the fact that the entire generation that came out of Egypt was to die in the wilderness because of their rebellion against the Lord.
Confirms that those who were numbered in the wilderness of Sinai died, except for Caleb and Joshua.
Describes Korah's rebellion, which Zelophehad's daughters explicitly state their father was not part of.
Tells of the punishment that struck Korah and his followers, among whom Zelophehad's father was not included.
Ezekiel describes the principle that whoever sins shall die for their own sin, which is reflected in the statement 'he died for his own sin'.
An example of dying for one's own sin, as Nadab and Abihu died for their sin when they offered unauthorized fire.
The context identifying Zelophehad's daughters and their lineage, explaining who speaks in this verse.
